name: James Covel
role: Methodist minister who covenanted to obey, then left
dateNote: Sections 39 and 40 were given on 5 and 6 January 1831 at Fayette.
importance: Section 39 tells a minister named James that he should be baptized and preach. Section 40, given a day later, says his heart had been right but fear and worldly cares led him to reject the word. Joseph Smith’s history says he returned to his former principles and people.
connections: He dealt with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon at Fayette. He had been a Methodist preacher for decades and helped ordain the first elders of the AME Zion Church in 1822.
reviewNote: JSP identifies him as the Methodist preacher James Covel (born about 1770, likely Massachusetts; died February 1850, New York City). The section 39 setting notes that no source fully settles his identity. Bare “James” in 39:7 is not linked.
